diagnosis.JANUS_ORBIT: The v1 independent-powmod collision strategy mostly recovers the known birthday-scale collision effect but pays O(log N)-like modular-multiplication cost per diversified exponent probe; strong BSGS reuses incremental group work and dominates total compute on this ladder.
diagnosis.GEMINI_V0: A second independent relation core provides an escape route (34/36 Fermat-style factor receipts) but naive parallel fusion adds compute and gives 0/35 total-compute wins versus the best successful single core.
diagnosis.MAD_LAB_target: Search for structures where exact cross-core hints reduce the other core's work; otherwise dual-core execution is compute tax rather than algorithmic synergy.

successor_requirements: ORBIT successor must reuse group transitions or otherwise amortize exponent probes instead of paying independent powmod per sample.
Any ORBIT improvement must still be compared against BSGS/rho, not linear scan.
GEMINI successor must demonstrate cross-core compression: an exact hint from one core must reduce the other core's measured work enough to overcome the donor-core cost.
MAD-LAB must maximize the best-successful-core gap and preserve counterexamples.
A polynomial-time factoring claim remains forbidden without a formal poly(log N) worst-case bit-complexity proof.
